A general view of scorched vehicles at the site of a strike in Bartalla after US-Saudi strikes on Iraq, in Nineveh Province, Iraq, July 29, 2026. 
Editor's note: Wang Jin is a Middle East expert from China's Northwest University. The article reflects the author's opinion and not necessarily the views of CGTN.
The conflict between the United States and Iran remains ongoing, while countries such as Yemen and Iraq have become increasingly drawn into the hostilities. As a result, the security situation across the Middle East continues to deteriorate.
Over the past two weeks, the geographical scope of the conflict has expanded significantly. Since the renewed outbreak of hostilities between the United States and Iran in July, tensions have escalated rapidly, with fighting resuming in Yemen and Iraqi Shiite militia groups becoming increasingly involved. The United States and Saudi Arabia have subsequently carried out strikes against militia targets inside Iraq. Coupled with the recent drone attack on Egypt, these developments suggest that the conflict is spreading across the region, with regional actors increasingly realigning their strategic positions.
A person watches Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Sarea delivering a televised statement in Sana'a, Yemen, July 25, 2026. 
The renewed confrontation between the United States and Iran has reignited long-standing regional tensions that had previously shown signs of easing. In Yemen, the dispute over flights from Sana'a International Airport became the immediate trigger for renewed confrontation. Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government argued that direct flights to Tehran violated the 2022 Yemen ceasefire agreement and could facilitate Iranian support for the Houthis. Flights between Iran and Sana'a on July 3 and July 13 further heightened these suspicions. The Houthis subsequently imposed a blockade in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, contributing to the renewed outbreak of hostilities.
The conflict has also drawn Iraq further into the regional crisis. Iraqi Shiite militias maintain close ties with Iran and have long been viewed by the United States and Gulf Arab states as important Iranian partners. After the renewed fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, Saudi Arabia accused Iraqi Shiite militias of assisting the Houthis and, together with the United States, carried out strikes against militia positions inside Iraq. Although the Iraqi central government has opposed unauthorized foreign military operations on its territory, it has struggled to exercise effective control over the militias, while the groups have denied involvement in attacks targeting Saudi Arabia. This has further exposed Iraq's political and factional divisions and increased the risk of cross-border escalation.
More importantly, the widening conflict has significantly strengthened regional states' sense of strategic vulnerability. Continued fighting in Iraq and Yemen has placed both the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea under mounting pressure, disrupting international shipping and raising concerns among Gulf Arab states and countries along the Red Sea coast.
The risks extend well beyond the region. Any blockade of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait would threaten navigation through the Suez Canal, while disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz could affect global energy supplies. Egypt, as the principal country responsible for safeguarding the Suez Canal, may therefore face difficult strategic choices and could be drawn more deeply into the conflict. At the same time, Ukraine's support for the US position suggests that the repercussions of the Middle East conflict are increasingly intersecting with the Russia-Ukraine conflict, highlighting the growing interaction between regional crises and broader international security challenges.
Iranians drive past a large political billboard at Valiasr Square in Tehran, Iran, August 1, 2026. 
Looking ahead, the conflict is likely to remain highly intense while continuing to expand geographically. The United States and Iran have yet to reach consensus on how the conflict should end, while fundamental differences remain over issues including the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's nuclear program. A negotiated settlement is therefore unlikely in the near term.
Meanwhile, the arrangements underpinning stability in Yemen and Iraq remain fragile. The 2022 Yemen ceasefire agreement and the political arrangements surrounding Shiite militia groups in Iraq are both vulnerable to renewed pressure as the wider conflict continues. Rather than containing the crisis, their deterioration could create new flashpoints and further worsen the regional security environment.
In the short term, although regional actors including Pakistan, Qatar, and Oman remain willing to play constructive mediation roles, the rapid expansion of the conflict has already pushed the crisis beyond the bilateral framework of US-Iran relations, reigniting long-standing regional disputes. Key international waterways, including the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and the Strait of Hormuz, are likely to remain vulnerable to disruption, posing serious risks to global energy production, transportation and supply chains. Consequently, achieving a comprehensive end to the conflict in the near future is likely to prove extremely difficult.
Over the medium to long-term, sustained international mediation and diplomatic coordination remain the most viable means of de-escalating the conflict. The key challenge for the international community will be to intervene promptly and effectively amid intensifying regional tensions, encourage the parties to manage existing disputes and prevent local confrontations from developing into a wider regional conflict. Its ability to do so will be a critical test of collective diplomatic capacity and the international community's ability to preserve regional stability.

paragraphs.en:
As people age, many experience memory decline and slower {{0}} processing, along with a higher risk of {{1}} disease and cognitive {{2}}. One important question in aging research is how changes in the brain's blood vessels contribute to cognitive decline. Scientists from the Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology (SIAT) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences have identified a {{3}} by which aging weakens the blood-brain barrier, the brain's protective {{4}} with the bloodstream. The study was published in Neuron under the title "TGF-β1-induced endothelial transcytosis drives blood-brain barrier {{6}} during aging."
The study shows how aging {{5}} {{16}} in brain blood vessel cells, leading to blood-brain barrier leakage. /SIAT
The blood-brain barrier, or BBB, acts as a {{7}} security system.
paragraphs.cn: 随着人们年龄增长，许多人会经历记忆力下降和认知处理速度变慢，同时脑血管疾病和认知障碍的风险也会增加。衰老研究中的一个重要问题是大脑血管的变化如何导致认知衰退。中国科学院深圳先进技术研究院（SIAT）的科学家们识别出衰老削弱血脑屏障（大脑与血流之间的保护性界面）的一种机制。该研究发表在《神经元》杂志上，标题为“TGF-β1诱导的内皮转胞吞作用驱动衰老过程中的血脑屏障渗漏”。该研究展示了衰老如何扰乱脑血管细胞中的运输，导致血脑屏障渗漏。/SIAT 血脑屏障（BBB）充当一个选择性的安全系统。

paragraphs.en: It allows {{8}} nutrients to reach the brain while preventing potentially harmful {{9}} in the blood from entering brain tissue. Damage to this barrier has been linked to cognitive aging, cerebral small vessel disease and several {{10}} disorders. Scientists have traditionally {{11}} BBB leakage mainly to damage to the tight seals between cells lining brain blood vessels. However, the new study found that another process occurs earlier during aging. As people age, many experience memory decline and slower cognitive processing, along with a higher risk of cerebrovascular disease and cognitive impairment. One important question in aging research is how changes in the brain's blood vessels contribute to cognitive decline.
Scientists from the Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology (SIAT) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences have identified a mechanism by which aging weakens the blood-brain barrier, the brain's protective interface with the bloodstream.
The study was published in Neuron under the title "TGF-β1-induced endothelial transcytosis drives blood-brain barrier leakage during aging."
The study shows how aging disrupts transport in brain blood vessel cells, leading to blood-brain barrier leakage. /SIAT
The blood-brain barrier, or BBB, acts as a selective security system. It allows essential nutrients to reach the brain while preventing potentially harmful substances in the blood from entering brain tissue. Damage to this barrier has been linked to cognitive aging, cerebral small vessel disease and several neurodegenerative disorders.
Scientists have traditionally attributed BBB leakage mainly to damage to the tight seals between cells lining brain blood vessels. However, the new study found that another process occurs earlier during aging.
By examining mice at different ages, the researchers found that BBB leakage was already detectable in middle-aged mice and worsened in older animals. The change appeared early in the hippocampus, a brain region important for learning and memory.
At this stage, the seals between blood vessel cells remained largely intact. Instead, the cells' internal transport system became abnormally active, allowing blood-borne substances to pass through the cells and enter brain tissue.
"Rather than first leaking through gaps between cells, the aging blood-brain barrier appears to lose control over transport pathways inside the cells," the researchers said.
The team identified a protein called Mfsd2a as an important part of this protective system. Mfsd2a normally limits unnecessary transport across brain blood vessels. Its levels declined with age, while Caveolin-1, a protein involved in the formation of transport vesicles, increased.
When the researchers restored endothelial Mfsd2a expression or knocked down Caveolin-1 in aged mice, abnormal vesicle transport and BBB leakage were significantly reduced.
The researchers then investigated why Mfsd2a declines during aging. They found that levels of TGF-β1, a signaling molecule involved in inflammation, tissue repair and aging, increased in both the brain and the bloodstream as mice aged.
Excessive TGF-β1 reduced Mfsd2a expression in the cells lining brain blood vessels, causing their transport activity to increase. Raising TGF-β1 levels in young mice caused them to develop several features normally seen in the aged BBB, including increased leakage.
By contrast, blocking TGF-β signaling in aged mice reduced BBB leakage and improved their performance in memory-related behavioral tests.
The findings suggest that age-related BBB damage is not simply the result of passive wear and tear. Instead, it involves biological signals that alter how brain blood vessel cells transport substances.
The study may help explain how vascular changes contribute to cognitive aging. It also points to potential approaches for protecting the aging brain, including maintaining Mfsd2a function or preventing excessive activation of TGF-β signaling. Further research will be needed to determine whether these strategies can be safely translated into treatments for humans.

The 25th China Internet Conference opens at the China National Convention Center in Beijing, capital of China, July 8, 2026. 
Artificial intelligence is moving rapidly from experimental technology to real-world applications, as industry leaders showcased new AI-powered solutions for cities, businesses and consumers at the 25th China Internet Conference in Beijing.
Held from July 8 to 10, the conference highlighted how AI agents, large language models and digital twin technologies are being integrated into sectors ranging from urban governance and industrial manufacturing to retail and public services.
Speaking via video at the opening ceremony, Wu Hequan, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering, said AI-native technologies are reshaping the internet itself.
While large language models excel at general reasoning, AI agents are designed to execute specific tasks and future digital ecosystems will increasingly rely on collaboration among multiple intelligent agents rather than isolated AI systems.
Participants of the 25th China Internet Conference try on VR products at the China National Convention Center in Beijing, capital of China, July 8, 2026. 
According to Wu, AI-generated traffic is expected to account for around 60% of global internet traffic by 2030, with AI agent services becoming the dominant source of token-based interactions. The shift, he said, will require internet infrastructure to evolve toward higher bandwidth, lower latency and stronger computing capabilities.
The conference also demonstrated how AI is being deployed in practical scenarios. Digital assistants are supporting office collaboration and customer services, while AI-powered inspection systems are improving industrial operations. Digital twin technologies are enabling more efficient traffic management, energy optimization and building maintenance, providing city managers with real-time visualization and decision-making tools.
Industry representatives also emphasized that AI innovation is creating measurable economic value.
Participants of the 25th China Internet Conference interact with humanoid robots at the China National Convention Center in Beijing, capital of China, July 8, 2026. 
At the conference, Kuaishou said its AI-powered video generation model and digital human live-streaming platform have helped small and medium-sized businesses increase daily gross merchandise value while significantly reducing marketing costs. Alibaba's Taobao Instant Commerce platform reported that AI agents are increasingly handling complex shopping requests, moving beyond traditional keyword-based searches to task-oriented consumer services.
Beyond applications, participants identified trustworthy AI and green computing as key priorities for the industry's next stage of development. The launch of the FlagOS Initiative, an open AI software platform designed to improve compatibility across different computing chips, reflects broader efforts to build more efficient and sustainable AI infrastructure.
As AI technologies continue to mature, industry experts believe the focus is shifting from developing models to deploying them at scale. The conference highlighted China's efforts to accelerate AI adoption across the real economy, with intelligent applications increasingly becoming part of everyday life while supporting digital transformation and high-quality economic development.

People gather at Bab Sebta, on the Morocco-Spain border near Spain's enclave of Ceuta and the Moroccan town of Fnideq, July 30, 2026. 
Spain's government on Thursday deployed armed forces stationed in the North African enclave of Ceuta to support the Civil Guard after thousands of migrants crossed into the territory from neighboring Morocco.
According to Spanish media reports, at least nine migrants died while attempting to reach the Spanish enclave by sea.
According to Spanish media reports, the armed forces will reinforce the Civil Guard in carrying out its duties and operate under the coordination of the Armed Forces' Operations Command.
Thousands of migrants entered Ceuta on Thursday, placing severe pressure on local reception facilities and security services.
Ceuta's regional leader Juan Jesus Vivas called on the central government to declare a national emergency and assume unified command of the response.
Spain's Interior Ministry said Spain and Morocco had agreed to strengthen coordination in response to the migration situation and accelerate procedures for the return of people who entered Ceuta illegally.
Spanish army soldiers are deployed to the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, July 30, 2026. 
European Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration Magnus Brunner said on social media platform X that the European Union stood ready to increase support for Spain, including through Frontex, and was also in contact with the Moroccan authorities to help prevent dangerous irregular crossings.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez and Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska are scheduled to visit Ceuta on Friday as the government steps up its response to the crisis.
Ceuta, together with Melilla, is one of Spain's two autonomous cities on the North African coast and forms the European Union's only land border with Africa.
The surge of migrant arrivals in Ceuta has been triggered primarily by a landmark ruling from Spain's Supreme Court.
The judgment banned the practice of summary "hot returns" for migrants intercepted at sea near the enclave, stripping authorities of the power to immediately send sea-borne irregular migrants back to Morocco without full individual legal procedures.
